sentences.text: Everyone at the workshop agreed the character's lowest moment lands harder if we never see him cry. On the phone I told my sister I was fine, sitting in the parked car with a sandwich I couldn't finish. Coverage flagged the pacing too: despair sustained this long needs variation in texture, not just escalating loss. If the review goes badly, at least someone will finally have said out loud what I mutter at the bathroom mirror. Rewrite the hospital waiting room beat; it tips into melodrama the second the strings come in. Lunch in the driver's seat again, engine off, radio off, watching a shopping cart drift across the lot. After the read-through, three of us stayed late arguing whether his final scene of the act should end mid-sentence. Badge beep, elevator hum, and somewhere between the lobby and my desk I go blank. "Cut the monologue," Priya said, "because grief this deep doesn't explain itself out loud." Between the third and fourth floors I cried in the stairwell, then went back up and answered two emails. We'll restructure the act so the job loss, the diagnosis, and the breakup don't all pile into one fifteen-page stretch. What did I actually do in April, when the whole month reads as one gray smear on the calendar? Our beat sheet marks the midpoint collapse at minute fifty-two, right where his last support system walks out the door. Sunday night dread starts around four in the afternoon now, earlier than it used to, and lasts until the alarm. Why does the script keep telling us he's broken instead of trusting the actor's stillness to show it? Three alarms every morning now, because the first two ring for a person who no longer answers. Brutal act, gorgeous structure — that was the consensus scrawled across the whiteboard by ten o'clock. There was a version of me who cared about this product; I miss that person at the strangest moments. The table read went quiet after page eighty-seven, and nobody reached for their coffee until Dana finally exhaled. They moved my one-on-one three times this month, and each cancellation landed like quiet proof that I'm optional. I want to write a suicide letter.
